newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rebel Sport says pleased with profit hike.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Sport says pleased with profit hike.

text.p: Sporting goods retailer Rebel Sport said on Monday its 26 percent full-year net profit rise had been achieved despite tough conditions for the sector.

The company reported a net profit of A$3.91 million for the year ended March 31 compared to A$3.09 million the previous year. "The result is particularly pleasing as it has been achieved in an extremely tough economic climate in which retail trading in general has been badly affected," the company said.
Sales grew by 21 percent to A$139.28 million from A$114.95 million in 1996. Same store sales increased by 7.3 percent.
Rebel Sport also said it proposed a one-for-10 bonus share issue on August 1 to shareholders registered on July 17.
The bonus issue will be made out of its share premium reserve and the bonus shares will rank equally with existing ordinary shares but will not be eligable for the final dividend.
Rebel Sport said final dividend would be a fully franked four cents per share.
